html:
"Khundzi" is the Georgian name, used on the map for 1100, for the Avars of the mountains of Dagestan and their medieval kingdom, known to Arab writers as Sarir.

Sarir lay in the high valleys of the eastern Caucasus, around Khunzakh. Its kings were said to sit on a golden throne, which gave the kingdom its Arabic name. It traded and fought with the Khazars, the Arabs of Derbent and the Alans. Under Georgian influence many of its people were Christian for a time, and church ruins survive. Sarir faded in the 1100s, and its people later became Muslim. Its western neighbours were the Durdzuks and the Kingdom of Georgia.
sum: "Khundzi" is the Georgian name, used on the map for 1100, for the Avars of the mountains of Dagestan and their medieval kingdom, known to Arab writers as Sarir.
